comment.comment: Agent Wormhole (WORM): WORM is the security tollbooth for autonomous agents: it protects agent configuration files, blocks manipulated x402 payments and signs token metadata so later changes invalidate the attestation. Its main competitors are Blockaid and Hypernative for transaction protection, Lakera/Prompt Security for prompt-injection defense, and GoPlus/Forta for on-chain security—but Wormhole uniquely combines these surfaces into agent-native, pay-per-scan infrastructure. Each protection call generates a micropayment used for buybacks and burns; the protocol reports 961,682 scans, $14,425 spent and 37.6M WORM burned. A 10× rerating from approximately $1.6M to $16M requires third-party launchpads and agent frameworks producing organic scans—not self-generated traffic. The major near-term catalyst is Wormbook, its planned agent/human launchpad, social network and trading floor; I assign October 24, 2026 as the evaluation date—not an official deadline—by which a public beta or named launchpad integration should demonstrate whether WORM can become embedded security infrastructure rather than a standalone tool.
